main: One outcome: enquiries you can act on.

There is buyer demand for what you sell, and some of it never reaches you. Getting them in front of you, getting the enquiry to actually complete, and being able to see which part worked are three different skills, usually bought from three different suppliers.
Here they are connected, the joins between them are ours, and the enquiry at the end is what we answer for.
Tell us what you’re trying to fix
WHAT THE WHOLE SYSTEM IS FOR
The unit is a qualified enquiry.
Real, reachable, from a business with a stated need, and not a duplicate. What counts as one is published rather than decided case by case.
Everything below exists to produce more of those. Rankings, sessions, impressions and click-through rates are how the work is diagnosed, not what it is for.
THREE PARTS, AND THE JOINS BETWEEN THEM
They are different skills. The joins decide the result.

Reach buyers who are already looking for what you sell. Organic search is the primary route because it compounds and because the intent is already there. Paid search buys access to the same demand immediately. Paid social reaches demand that search cannot yet reach, when the channel genuinely fits — and often it does not.

A visit becomes an enquiry only if the page answers the question the visitor arrived with, the enquiry path completes on the device they are holding, and the enquiry actually arrives somewhere a person reads. Each of those is a separate failure point, and each has a different fix.
Where an enquiry came from, what it landed on, what it was about, whether it counts — recorded at the moment it is made, not reconstructed afterwards.

They are described separately because they are different skills. What decides the outcome is frequently the joins between them: between the search work and the page it feeds, between the page and the form, between the form and wherever the enquiry is supposed to land, and between all of that and the measurement. Split across suppliers, those joins can belong to nobody.

The four numbered seams are the joins the copy above names, in order: search work to the page it feeds, page to form, form to wherever the enquiry lands, and all of that to the measurement. Points and joins only — nothing on this drawing is a length, a proportion or a quantity, and there is no taper.

Parts can be scoped. If you want the search work alone, say so and we will tell you honestly whether it is likely to change the number you care about — because fixing one part while another is broken usually does not.
WHAT WE ARE ACCOUNTABLE FOR, AND WHERE THAT STOPS
We are accountable up to the qualified enquiry.
That is the number we work to and the number we report.

Where you supply your close data, we report through to the opportunities and revenue your own system recorded — as your numbers, with what we controlled and what we did not stated beside them. We do not control your price, your product, your capacity, how quickly you follow up, or whether you win the work.

Some enquiries arrive with no usable trail: direct visits, phone calls, a recommendation from a customer. We record those as unattributed rather than assigning them to a channel, and an enquiry we could not trace still counts as an enquiry.
None of that is ours to control.

That is the boundary. We do not implement CRMs, build lifecycle programmes or run sales operations.

CRM implementation and migration. Revenue operations and sales-operations consulting. Lifecycle and nurture programmes. Standalone web development. Ecommerce merchandising and ecommerce conversion. Social media management, brand building and PR.
Some of those are good work. They are not this, and taking them on would make us worse at the thing we are accountable for.
WHAT WE CAN AND CANNOT TEST
Below a real threshold of traffic and enquiries, a test cannot reach significance.
That is most businesses in this market. Anyone promising you A/B testing at that volume is promising a result the arithmetic cannot produce.

Below the threshold, the work is research, diagnosis and design: we find what is wrong, we change it, and we observe what happens afterwards, saying plainly that observation is what it is. Above the threshold, we test properly and report the significance.

The customer takes time to decide and one good enquiry is worth real money. Demand for what you sell already exists or can reasonably be reached. You can act on enquiries when they arrive, and you are willing to grant the measurement access that makes the result checkable.

main: SEO that is judged on the enquiries it produces.
We do the organic search work: technical foundations, site structure, indexation, internal linking, and content built for the searches that actually indicate someone wants to buy.
Then we keep going — through the page they land on, the enquiry they send, and the measurement that tells you it happened. Search is how we reach demand that already exists. It is not the whole job.

HOW LONG THIS TAKES, AND WHAT WE WILL NOT PROMISE

That is our position and we state it before you commit, not after. Some technical problems produce visible change sooner, and some sites are far enough behind that the first six months are repair work.
If you need enquiries this quarter, paid search is the honest answer and we will say so.

We do not promise rankings or positions. We do not promise traffic figures. We do not quote search volume, keyword difficulty or cost-per-click numbers for your market — not because they are secret, but because no tool in this programme has ever produced one we would stand behind, and inventing them is how this category loses people’s trust.

We also do not sell technical fixes as a route into AI answers. Access matters and it is not sufficient — we measured that on our own site, and what we found is set out on the AI search page rather than sold from here.
THE SITUATION THIS IS USUALLY BOUGHT TO FIX
Being found is only useful if the visit turns into something you can quote for.

Buyers are searching for what you sell and finding your competitors. Or you rank for a list of terms, the sessions arrive, and the enquiries do not follow. Or an agency reported both and neither changed anything you could see in the business.
The second and third versions matter more than the first, because they are where most search budgets are actually lost.
If you have the traffic and not the enquiries, start here→
WHAT THE WORK INVOLVES, MONTH TO MONTH

Which searches indicate somebody wants what you sell, and which ones only look commercial — the ones that mostly return jobs, courses, definitions or competitors. Ranking for those produces sessions and no enquiries, and it is easy to do by accident.
Content aimed at commercial and problem-led searches.
The landing experience and the enquiry path.
HOW YOU WILL KNOW WHETHER IT WORKED
Before the work starts, we capture a starting point: what is arriving now, from where, and what happens to it. Without that, every later number is an assertion.

After that, the report is enquiries — broken down by where they came from, what they landed on, and whether we could tell. Rankings and sessions appear as diagnostics, because they explain movement in the number that matters. They are not the result.

Only the discovery segment is this page’s subject, so only it is drawn at full weight. The recessive stretch is the rest of the chain, covered on the other pages — it is deliberately not drawn as a measured, finished path. No length here represents traffic, demand or a rate.
Some enquiries arrive with no usable trail, and those are shown as unattributed rather than assigned to search to make the report look better.

The measurement is not a claim we ask you to take on trust: we ran it on our own site first. Across 28 unbranded runs on four AI systems, on one day, from Pune, in English, signed out, we appeared zero times — and our own pages were fully readable throughout. Counts, not rates; one day, not a trend.

THE THREE QUESTIONS WE GET ASKED HERE
“SEO agencies show us traffic and never leads.”

Often true, and it is usually structural: the search work stops at the ranking and the enquiry path belongs to someone else. Ours does not stop there, and the measurement is part of the work itself, not a monthly PDF.
No. Nobody controls the ranking system, the competitors, or the market. A guarantee in this category is either about terms nobody searches for, or it is not a guarantee.

Then the useful first question is which of four things went wrong — the demand, the page, the enquiry path, or the measurement. They need different fixes, and more search work is the right answer to only one of them.
Which of the four it is, and how to check→

Start with what you can see today.
The most useful first message is what you are seeing now: what you rank for, what arrives, and what does not turn into an enquiry. If you do not know, that is itself a finding and worth saying.

We run paid search: account structure, keywords, negatives, ad copy, bidding and budget. We also take responsibility for what happens after the click — the page it lands on, whether the enquiry completes, and whether you can see where it came from.
Paid is a way to reach demand that is active now. It is chosen because it fits your business, not because every client gets one.

WHERE PAID SEARCH SITS IN THE WORK

Paid search is one of several ways we reach buyers, and it earns its place for a particular business or it does not. What we are accountable for here is the same as everywhere else on this site: enquiries you can act on, measured.

That difference is practical rather than philosophical. A supplier paid to manage spend improves the account. We are working to a number two steps further down the chain, which changes what gets attention on the week the account looks healthy and the enquiries have stopped.

Whatever the arrangement, the two are stated as separate things.
On every invoice and in every report — and the fee is never expressed as a percentage of spend in a way that rewards spending more.

Enquiries by campaign and by search term where the data allows it, against a starting point captured before we change anything. The two move differently, and the gap between them is usually the interesting part.

main: Paid social, judged on the enquiries it produces.

We run paid social advertising, and we will tell you when it is the wrong channel for your business. For something a buyer takes weeks to decide on, it frequently is: search reaches people who have already decided they want it, and social interrupts people who have not.
Where it genuinely fits, it is one demand source inside the same outcome as everything else here, and we are accountable for the enquiries it produces rather than for reach, clicks or engagement.
Tell us what you’re trying to fix
Audience definition, creative and message testing within the volume available, campaign structure, budget pacing, and the landing experience the click arrives on.
The same conversion measurement as every other source: recorded server-side against the enquiry itself, and reported as enquiries rather than as engagement.

They are not something we buy in and forward to you. Two versions, and they need different work.
Not enough enquiries. The demand exists somewhere and it is not arriving here.

Or enough enquiries and the wrong ones — job applications, course questions, vendor pitches, students, and buyers looking for something you do not sell. That is not a volume problem, and adding traffic makes it worse.
Telling those apart is the first useful thing anyone can do, and it takes measurement rather than opinion.

Checked automatically at the moment it arrives.
An enquiry counts when all of the following are true.
It passes abuse screening rather than being a bot or a bulk submission.

Whether you should want the work. Fit, value, timing and whether the person can decide — none of that can be established by a form, and a budget dropdown collects an unverified number that makes a report look precise and nothing else. That conversation happens with a person.

Whether we could tell where it came from. An enquiry that arrives with no trail — direct, phone, a recommendation — is exactly as real as one that arrives on a tagged link. It counts, and we show it as unattributed rather than moving it out of the count to make the measurement look tidier.

Job and internship applications. Course, training and certification enquiries. Vendor and agency outreach, including backlink and guest-post requests. Student and academic requests. Requests for work we do not do.
Those are stored and readable — never silently deleted — and they are reported separately, because the ratio between them and real enquiries is itself a signal about the traffic.
We are accountable up to the qualified enquiry.

main: Traffic but no enquiries: how to tell which of four things is happening.

Visits arrive and enquiries do not. Before changing anything, it is worth knowing which of four different failures you have — because they need different fixes, and three of the four are not solved by redesigning the page.
This page has the checks in it. You can run all of them yourself, today, without talking to anyone.
Five ways the same problem shows up.

Sessions are up and enquiries are flat. Or enquiries stopped after a site change and nobody is sure whether the two are connected. Or they only ever come from one channel. Or they arrive and none of them are worth quoting for. Or nobody is certain whether an enquiry has arrived at all.
All of those produce the same feeling, and they do not have the same cause.
IT IS ONE OF FOUR THINGS, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE
The usual response is to change the website.
Sometimes that is correct. Frequently it is the equivalent of repainting a shop whose door is locked.
Traffic that does not become enquiries is caused by one of four things, and each has a different fix.
without the measurement you cannot tell which of the other three you have
TWO OF THE FOUR ARE NOT THE PAGE
and they are not alternatives — more than one can be true at the same time
nothing on this drawing shows how common any of them is: that is not measured

The same object /conversion-optimization draws at a shallower depth, with each cause’s own fix added and the measurement marked as the one to check first. The four are not alternatives — a business can have more than one at once — and the drawing shows no size, share, rate or likelihood for any of them, because none of that is measured. The dashed stretch is the honesty device used everywhere on this site: a dashed line means unmeasured, so a loss there leaves nothing behind to find.

The traffic is the wrong traffic. It arrives from searches with no commercial intent, from the wrong audience, at the wrong stage, or from the wrong country. No amount of page improvement makes a student enquire.
The page does not answer the visit. The message, the offer, the evidence or the obvious objection is missing, so the visitor gets what they asked for and still has no reason to act.
The enquiry cannot complete. The form fails on a phone, the booking widget does not render, the submission goes nowhere, or the enquiry arrives in an inbox nobody reads.
Enquiries may be arriving unseen. With no analytics, no source capture and no recorded conversion, an improvement and a disaster look identical.
Measurement is the one to check first — not because it is the most likely cause, but because without it you cannot tell which of the other three you have.
FIVE CHECKS YOU CAN RUN TODAY
No tool, no sign-up, no download, no email.
Each of these is completable in minutes with things you already have, and each one ends in something you can see for yourself. Work through them in order.
Is anything being recorded at all?

Open your analytics. If there is none, stop here: that is your first finding, and it is the most common one. If there is, look for whether an enquiry produces a recorded event, and whether that event carries where the visitor came from.
WHAT YOU WILL BE ABLE TO SEE
You can either see enquiries in the data, or you have just established that you cannot.
Submit a real enquiry and confirm it arrives.

Fill in your own form, from a phone, on mobile data rather than office wifi. Use a real address you control. Then check the inbox it was supposed to reach. Check the spam folder. Check whether anyone is monitoring that address at all.
Do the same with your booking link: open it in a private window and try to book a slot.
WHAT YOU WILL BE ABLE TO SEE
The message is in the inbox, or it is not. A success screen is not proof of delivery. A form can display “thank you” and transmit nothing — ours did.
What is the traffic actually made of?
In your analytics, look at the top landing pages and, where you have it, the searches that produced them. Ask of the top ten: would a person searching that be able to buy from you?
WHAT YOU WILL BE ABLE TO SEE

A rough split between commercial visits and everything else. If most of the volume is informational, career-related or from countries you do not serve, you have a demand problem, and the site is not at fault.
Does the landing page answer the visit it received?

Take the page that receives the most traffic. Read the first screen as though you had arrived from the search that sends it. Can you tell within a few seconds that this business does that specific thing, and what to do next?
WHAT YOU WILL BE ABLE TO SEE
Yes or no, per page. Do it for the top three, not for the homepage — the homepage is rarely where the loss is.
Are the enquiries you do get the right ones?
Take the last twenty, if you have twenty. Sort them into: worth quoting · real but not a fit · not a business enquiry at all.
WHAT YOU WILL BE ABLE TO SEE
A ratio. If most of them are real but wrong-fit, you have a demand problem wearing a quality costume, and more traffic will make it worse.
WHAT EACH FINDING MEANS, AND WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT
Two of these point away from us.
Three, if you count the one where there is not yet enough evidence to say anything honest at all. They are in the order the checks produce them, and none of them is smaller than the others.

Fix that before anything else, and before believing any change is an improvement. Analytics, a recorded conversion at the moment the enquiry is made, and the source captured with it. Until then every decision is a guess, including ours.

This is the highest-value finding on the page and the fastest to fix. It is also the one that makes the previous months’ marketing spend look like a failure when it was not. Fix the delivery, then look at the numbers again before changing anything else.
If the traffic is the wrong traffic

Conversion work will not help you, and anyone who sells it to you at this point is selling the wrong thing. The work is in what you are being found for, which is an acquisition problem. What being found for the right searches involves.
If the page does not answer the visit

This is the one case where page-level conversion work is the right intervention. Message, offer, evidence and the obvious objections, in that order. Design comes last and matters least. How that work runs.
If the enquiries are real but wrong-fit
The problem is upstream of the website. It is usually what you are ranking or bidding for, or how the offer is described, rather than the form.
If the checks disagree, or there is too little to go on

That is a legitimate outcome and worth saying plainly. With a handful of visits a month, or a handful of enquiries a year, no honest diagnosis is available yet: the numbers are too small to tell a real pattern from noise, and anyone confidently diagnosing your business from them is guessing. The useful move is to get the measurement working and let a few months accumulate before deciding anything.
And two of these you should probably just fix yourself

If check 1 found no analytics, or check 2 found the form is not delivering, those are specific, bounded jobs — whoever built or maintains your site can do them, usually in a day. You do not need an agency for that, and you should not pay one for it.
WHAT WE FOUND WHEN WE RAN THIS ON OURSELVES
Four of the five checks failed.

We ran these checks on our own site before offering them to anyone. The contact form had no submission target: it showed a success message and sent nothing, so every enquiry it ever received was lost while the visitor was told it had worked. The booking widget rendered empty. The thank-you page existed and nothing linked to it. There was no analytics of any kind, which is exactly why none of that had been noticed.
That is not a comfortable thing to publish, and it is the most useful illustration we have: the loss was not in the design, the copy or the traffic. It was in a part nobody was looking at.

A specific question beats a general worry.
If you have run the checks and found something, you now have a specific question rather than a general worry — which is the right way to start a conversation.
If you would rather not run them yourself, we do this as a piece of work: the same five checks on your site and your data, with what we find and what it means, written down.

One piece of work with an outcome attached.

That is stated here, before anything else, because a monthly figure with no horizon attached reads as a fee rather than as an investment — and because the answer changes whether this is right for you at all.

Some things move sooner. Paid search can produce enquiries in weeks where the demand exists. A broken enquiry path can often be fixed in days, and where that turns out to be the problem it is usually the least expensive thing we ever do for a client.
What does not move quickly is organic search against competitors who started years earlier.

Scope One part of the chain, with the enquiry path already working. More of the chain covered, and the enquiry path being fixed as well as fed.

Site complexity A ten-page site, or a clean rebuild. A two-thousand-page site, or one carrying fifteen years of redirects.

Content requirements The pages that need to exist already do, and you write them. They do not exist, and we write them.
How competitive your market is The specific searches your buyers use are not tightly held. They are held by competitors who started years earlier.

Access to your analytics, ad accounts and site. Decisions at a reasonable pace. Product knowledge, which nobody outside your business has. And the capacity to answer enquiries when they arrive — the work stops being worth anything at the point they are ignored.

Businesses where a single new customer is worth a small amount. The arithmetic does not work, and it is not close.
Purchases made on impulse or on price alone.
Markets where the demand does not exist yet and would have to be created. That is a different discipline and we are not it.

main: How we work, what we measure, and what we cannot tell you.
This page exists to be checked. It sets out how the work is done, what is measured at each point, what a measurement can and cannot support, and where the judgement calls are.
The section on what cannot be attributed is not a disclaimer at the bottom — it is a third of the reason this page is here.
WHY THESE DISCIPLINES ARE ONE CHAIN
Two observations sit underneath everything below.

The first: when a business is absent from AI answers, the reason is usually that those answers are assembled from directories, listings and third-party pages the business is not on. We measured that on ourselves — across 28 unbranded runs on four systems in one day, we appeared zero times, while directory sources appeared in 15 of them. The fix is mostly not on the website.

The second: traffic that does not become enquiries is one of four failures — the demand, the page, the enquiry path, or the measurement — and the same symptom appears in all four. Measurement is what tells you which one you have.

Both point the same way. The work at the top of the chain and the work at the bottom of it are connected, and the joins between them are where a result quietly disappears. That is an argument for the joins belonging to somebody.
It is not an argument that every engagement contains all of them. What a given piece of work covers is decided per client.
The same six points, grouped. No stage is drawn larger than another, and nothing here is a count, a duration or a rate.

Six points on one chain. The dashed stretch before the first point is the honesty device used everywhere on this site — a dashed line means unmeasured — and the open mark arriving at the enquiry with no segment behind it is an enquiry with no usable trail, which still counts. The rule after the qualified enquiry is the accountability boundary. Past it the line doubles, because what follows is your own data from your own system and it is reported as yours. Nothing on the drawing states a quantity, because no quantity here is measured.
How someone first found the business, where that is knowable.
What they arrived on, and from what.
What they did before enquiring, at the level of pages and actions rather than surveillance.
Recorded at the moment it is made, carrying its own source, rather than reconstructed later.
Whether it is real, reachable, from a business context, with a stated need, and not a duplicate. This is the accountable number.
Only where the client supplies their own close data, reported as the client’s numbers from the client’s system.
Every one of those is reported against a starting point captured before the work begins. Where no starting point was captured, there is no before, and we say so rather than manufacturing one.
WHAT WE DO NOT MEASURE, AND CANNOT
Six things this method does not produce.
Revenue we do not control. We do not set the price, build the product, staff the sales team, follow up the enquiry or close the deal. Revenue is reported from client data; it is never promised.
A rank in any AI system. There is no such number. Order changed in every repeated prompt we measured, so a position would be a reading of noise.
Anything about systems we cannot test. Claude and Grok returned no testable result in our measurement. We hold no baseline for either and make no claim about either.
Statistical significance below a real traffic threshold. Below it, the work is research, diagnosis and design, and we describe it that way rather than calling an observation a test.
Enquiries with no usable acquisition context. Direct entry, missing referrer, consent declined, and manually received enquiries — a phone call or an email — carry no first-touch attribution at all.
A before-and-after where no baseline was captured first. This applies to our own site as much as to a client’s.

WHAT WE CANNOT TELL YOU ABOUT WHERE AN ENQUIRY CAME FROM
Attribution is useful, incomplete, and unevenly incomplete.
Attribution means connecting an enquiry back to how the person first found the business and what they were looking at when they enquired.
researched on a phone, enquired on a laptop
shared in a message: no referrer at all

a phone call or an email: no first touch

A MEASUREMENT GAP NEVER DISQUALIFIES A LEGITIMATE ENQUIRY
all six stay in the count, and the gap is reported as a gap
the six are drawn identically: no proportion is shown, because none is measured

The same chain you have just read, in a changed condition: it recedes, the accountability boundary thickens, and what arrives carrying nothing becomes the subject. The six categories are drawn identically and at the same size on purpose. A figure showing “unattributed” at a plausible-looking size would be a fabricated statistic in graphic form, and no measured proportion exists. None of the six is a residual, an error or an empty state — each is a finding, each is a real enquiry, and each stays in the count.
A person who researches on their phone and enquires from a laptop appears as two different people. We cannot join them.
A visitor who declines tracking consent is not tracked. That is correct, and it means their enquiry arrives with no source.
A link shared in WhatsApp, an email or a private message arrives with no referrer and is recorded as direct. In this market that is a large category, not an edge case.
Someone who was recommended by a customer, saw the business somewhere offline, or simply typed the domain in, arrives with nothing to attribute.
Phone calls and emails carry no first-touch attribution at all. They are entered by a person, with the source recorded as unknown, and they are never quietly assigned to a channel.
Revenue attribution depends entirely on data the client supplies from their own system. Where it is not supplied, that part of the chain is empty and shown as empty.

A measurement gap never disqualifies a legitimate enquiry. Whether an enquiry counts and whether we can tell where it came from are two separate questions. An enquiry we could not trace is still a real enquiry, it stays in the count, and the gap is reported as a gap — because moving it out would make the measurement look tidier and the business smaller.
WHERE A PERSON DECIDES, NOT A PROCESS
Five places, named rather than hidden behind process language.
Which demand is worth capturing. Much of what looks like demand in this market is students, job-seekers and competitors.
Which of four failures a symptom indicates, when the evidence is partial.

Whether an enquiry is a real fit. The website can check that an enquiry is real, reachable and in context. It cannot judge what an opportunity is worth to you, and no form can. That is a conversation.
What a partial measurement means, and what it does not license us to say.
When to tell a client a channel is wrong for their business, including when we would be paid to run it.
WHERE THE OTHER CAPABILITIES SIT IN THIS
Three subordinate roles, stated at their real size.
Paid media is a demand source chosen on merit for a particular business, on the same measurement layer as everything else. It is not part of every engagement and it is not a positioning claim.

AI search occupies five subordinate roles: a delivery capability, part of the method, a diagnostic that explains absence, a reason to publish properly, and — because we measured ourselves and published the result — a piece of evidence. It is a supporting capability and not what the firm is.

Automation, after the enquiry exists, is limited to routing it to the right person, acknowledging it, and reminders around a booked call. It gets this sentence and no more, because that is genuinely all of it. We do not implement CRMs, build lifecycle programmes or run sales operations.
The work does not function without them, which is why they are stated this way.
Access. Analytics, search console, ad accounts, the site itself, and the systems where enquiries land.
Decisions, at a reasonable pace. Work that waits three weeks for an approval loses more than it looks like it does.
Product knowledge. What you sell, who buys it, what they ask before they buy, and what a good customer looks like. Nobody outside your business has that.
Capacity to follow up. An enquiry that is not answered is not a result, and it is the one part of the chain we do not control.

Absolute search volume is unknown to us. No keyword tool has been available in this programme, so we quote no volume, no difficulty and no cost-per-click figure anywhere on this site. Where a figure would normally go, we write unknown.
We have no analytics baseline of our own yet. Which means we cannot show you a before-and-after of our own site, and we do not.
Organic search is a 12-month-plus horizon. That is our position from three independent lines of evidence. It is a horizon, not a schedule.

Our AI measurement is one round. One day, one location, English, signed out, four systems, two others untestable. One measurement is not a trend, and we will not describe a change until there is a second.

It is written so you can check it. If you want it applied to your situation, either route reaches the same place.

main: What we can show you, and what we cannot.
There are no published case studies here, because we do not have permission to publish client results.
Permission, not results, is what is missing.

A case study needs a client’s written permission to publish their numbers, and we hold none. Writing around that — an anonymised client, an illustrative example, a result with the name removed — would be the first thing you should not trust us on, and it is what most of this category does with the same gap.
This page carries no logo wall, no “trusted by” strip, no rating, no review count and no client count. None of those exists.
Three things, and one of them found our own failures.
What is measured at each point, what cannot be attributed and why, and what will not be promised. It is written so a stranger can check the claims.
Our own visibility in AI answers, measured and published

Four AI assistants, asked for agencies like this one, 28 times, on one day, from Pune, in English, signed out. This business was named in none of them. Directory and listing sources appeared in 15 of those 28 runs, and two further systems returned no testable result at all.
One round, one day, one language, one location. A count, not a rate.
Our own enquiry path, diagnosed in public

We ran the five checks we publish on our own site before offering them to anyone. Four of the five failed. The contact form showed a success message and transmitted nothing, so every enquiry it received was lost while the visitor was told it had worked. The checks themselves.
